description: The CBE Thermal Comfort Tool is a web application developed by the University of California, Berkeley for comfort calculations and visualisation. It implements PMV/PPD, SET, adaptive and local-discomfort models, with additional solar-gain and clothing calculations. Inputs describe temperatures, air movement, humidity, clothing and activity; users can also upload time series for batch calculations and exceedance analysis. Outputs include comfort indices and interactive psychrometric or adaptive charts. Coverage is globally configurable for indoor conditions, with temporal detail inherited from the supplied observations or simulations. The hosted tool is free, and repository source is available under GPL-2.0. A limitation is the stated applicability range of each comfort method, including restrictions on clothing, activity and occupant conditions. The application can assess comfort in building-control simulations, complementary to EnergyPlus (model-energyplus). Official documentation and the live interface identify its models, batch workflow and SoftwareX 2020 citation. This is a different resource from CBE's Clima weather-analysis tool. No measurements were uploaded and no individual health assessment was performed.
